parole.significato: goat buck, billy goat, ram (a male goat)
parole.testo: Unknown. Probably from Paleo-Hispanic. Or, possibly of Germanic origin, borrowed through Spanish bode.

parole.significato: gourd (cultivated plant, used as vegetable or container)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese cabaaça, from earlier *cabalaça, possibly metathised from local latin *calapatia via Paleo-Hispanic. Cognate with Galician cabaza, Spanish calabaza and Catalan carabassa.

parole.significato: holm oak (Quercus ilex, a tree of the Mediterranean)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Paleo-Hispanic root, or perhaps from Latin cerrus (“Turkey oak”) + -asco.

parole.significato: a terrapin, or any other freshwater turtle
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese, from Paleo-Hispanic *calap(p)acu, perhaps related to the etymon of cabaça. Cognate with Galician cágado (“tadpole”), Spanish galápago (“turtle”) and Catalan calàpet (“toad”). Doublet of Galápagos.

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; Possibly; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: butter (fatty and unctuous substance obtained from the cream of milk)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese manteiga, of uncertain origin. Possibly from Paleo-Hispanic such as Iberian or Celtiberian. Cognate with Galician and Mirandese manteiga, Asturian and Catalan mantega, Spanish and Aragonese manteca and possibly with Proto-Slavic *sъmetana (“sour cream”).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; Probably; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: thicket (dense, small growth of shrubs, bushes or small trees)
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin. Compare with Galician mouta (“bush, hillock, dune, etc.”), probably from Paleo-Hispanic.

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese çarron of uncertain origin. Maybe from Paleo-Hispanic (compare Basque zorro (“sack”)). Cognate with Galician zurrón, Mirandese çurron, Asturian and Spanish zurrón.
Uncertain. Theories include: * from Paleo-Hispanic; * from Spanish tueca.

parole.significato: gorse; furze (Ulex europaeus, an evergreen shrub of Europe and northern Africa)
parole.testo: From Paleo-Hispanic *toju or similar; compare Spanish tojo, Asturian toxu, Galician toxo.
Assumed to be from a Paleo-Hispanic substrate. In any case, likely of imitative origin.

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; Possibly; perhaps; alternatively; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: broa (type of cornbread made in Portugal, Galicia and Brazil)
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese borõa, of uncertain origin. Possibly from Gothic *𐌱𐍂𐌰𐌿𐌸 (*brauþ, “bread”), from Proto-Germanic *braudą (“cooked food, leavened bread”). Alternatively, perhaps from Paleo-Hispanic. See that entry for more. Compare Galician broa.
Unknown. Possibly from a pre-Roman Paleo-Hispanic substrate, or from North Germanic/Scandinavian flark. Compare Spanish charco, from which it could have been borrowed.

From Paleo-Hispanic (compare Basque sasi, earlier çarzi). Alternatively, from Arabic شَرَا (šarā, “plant with thorns”), from سَارَاسَا (sārāsā, “to be evil, vicious”). Cognate with Asturian, Spanish, and Ladino zarza.

parole.significato: auger (tool for boring holes in wood)
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese traado (13th century), from Late Latin taratrum (“auger”), attested by Isidore of Seville. Either from Paleo-Hispanic or from Gaulish, from Proto-Celtic *taratrom, from Proto-Indo-European *térh₁-tro-. Alternatively from Ancient Greek τέρετρον (téretron, “borer, gimlet”)
